objective: Durable Job + Workflow Core (C-19), delivered as five atomic packages: the durable-job persistence foundation with two identities in one store and checkpoint ordering as identity; the durability semantics (execution attempts with ownership and heartbeat, row-derived retry accounting against a bound recorded on the job, an absolute per-attempt deadline, cancellation and dead-lettering); the job-type contract registry that makes ARK-REQ-0060's applicability rule mechanically evaluable, plus pause/resume and the crash-recovery sweep, both converging on the canonical RESUMING state because the Job relation gives it exactly two predecessors; the ARK-REQ-0027 enqueue surface under surfaces.command, where an HTTP request persists durable work and returns a reference without executing it; and this final integration, fault-injection evidence, traceability and acceptance submission. The canonical Job state machine delivered at Phase 3 remained the sole lifecycle authority throughout and nothing was added to it: RUNNING -> RECOVERABLE is not a declared edge, so crash recovery travels RUNNING -> FAILED -> RECOVERABLE -> RESUMING, which is the disposition Package 2 already owned. No scheduler, worker, workflow or provider functionality was implemented - C-21 is Phase 8 and C-20 is Phase 17.
public_contracts: C-19 durable job record + checkpoint - docs/contracts/job.md. Records: durable_job (job_id PK, job_type, idempotency_key, lifecycle_state, payload JSON, max_attempts, attempt_timeout_seconds, heartbeat_timeout_seconds, created_at, updated_at; unique (job_type, idempotency_key) named uq_durable_job_idempotency), job_checkpoint (job_id PK/FK, sequence PK, payload JSON, recorded_at; update and delete both refused at the ORM), job_execution_attempt (job_id PK/FK, attempt PK, owner, started_at, heartbeat_at, deadline_at, ended_at, outcome, detail), durable_job_type (job_type PK, supports_pause, registered_at). Public authority: JobStore (get/require/find_submitted/checkpoints/next_checkpoint_sequence/submit/transition/checkpoint), JobExecution (attempts/attempt_count/current_attempt/retry_permitted/timed_out/begin_attempt/heartbeat/complete_attempt/fail_attempt/time_out/cancel), JobTypeRegistry (get/require/supports_pause/declared/declare), JobRecovery (pause/resume/heartbeat_stale/recover_lost_executions). lifecycle_state is a recorded value; the canonical Job machine is the only transition authority.

arkali.surfaces.command.jobs - the ARK-REQ-0027 enqueue surface. POST /api/jobs (EnqueueJobRequest -> 202 JobReferenceResponse) persists durable work through C-19 and returns; GET /api/jobs/{job_id} resolves a reference. The response carries job_id, job_type, idempotency_key, lifecycle_state and created_at and nothing executional. Both routes declare the backend-only audience; no frontend obligation exists because no Phase 7 requirement is owned by a surface context.

arkali.surfaces.command.contracts.TransportModel - the base that normalises every datetime crossing this boundary to UTC-aware, so one persisted instant has one wire representation whether or not the row is still in the session (F-0038).
state_machine_capability_changes: NONE. The canonical Job machine delivered at Phase 3 was read before each package and found sufficient every time; no state, transition, forbidden pair or terminal state was added, removed or altered, and test_canonical_reconciliation.py still reconciles the implemented relation against STATE_MACHINES.md section 3. Three properties Phase 7 relies on are consequences of that unchanged relation rather than of code: RESUMING has exactly two predecessors (PAUSED and RECOVERABLE), so pause and crash recovery share one lifecycle meaning; RUNNING -> RECOVERABLE is NOT declared and evaluate refuses it, so recovery must travel through FAILED; and DEAD_LETTER has no outgoing transition, so a dead-lettered job cannot be revived by any sweep. No capability graph node was activated: capability resolution remains NOT_CONFIGURED and Phase 7 neither uses nor claims it.

duplicate_shadow_check: No duplicate or shadow authority was created. The canonical Job machine is the sole lifecycle authority: no module in execution.durable restates a state literal or a transition pair, the lifecycle column is assigned in exactly one method (derived as the one that calls evaluate, not named), and RESUMING is requested by exactly one module with every use of the name proven to be a transition target. Persistence has one authority: no engine is constructed or even imported in execution.durable or in the jobs router, and no raw or dialect-specific SQL appears in either. Evidence has one authority pair: Phase 7 evidence is recorded through evidence.artifact and evidence.audit unchanged, and no second evidence mechanism was created. security_findings: No security finding. Every governed operation in execution.durable and surfaces.command passes an injected PEP that has no default, so a caller cannot obtain a service that writes without a policy decision. Only two operation classes are requested - READ_FILE and WRITE_WORKSPACE_FILE - imported from the context whose operations they govern rather than restated, and unmapped_action_resolution: DENY means no new class could be invented. WRITE_STABLE_FILE and ROLLBACK_STABLE appear nowhere in either context and structure check 11 asserts it. A real PDP loaded from an authority map with WRITE_WORKSPACE_FILE fixed to DENY was driven through every governed path - submit, declare, pause, resume, the recovery sweep and the HTTP enqueue route - and each refusal was proven to leave the durable state unchanged. F-0039 was found and closed during the phase: PolicyDenied was mapped to 403 but unreachable from any route because guard() runs before the try, so a real denial surfaced as HTTP 500. Nothing failed open - the PEP still refused and nothing was written - but the client could not distinguish a refusal from a server fault; the mapping is now reachable from anywhere a domain error can be raised. The enqueue surface leaks no traceback, path, URL or SQL in any refusal, asserted.
